conversation:
Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today?
Patient: I'm 76 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here to establish care with you because I had a lumpectomy last year for ductal carcinoma in situ in my right breast. I'm feeling good overall, but I want to make sure I'm being properly followed up on.
Doctor: Could you please provide your height, weight, and any current medications or supplements you are taking?
Patient: I'm 76 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here to establish care with you because I had a lumpectomy last year for ductal carcinoma in situ in my right breast. I'm feeling good overall, but I want to make sure I'm being properly followed up on.
Doctor: Could you please provide details about your current medications, supplements, and any symptoms or concerns related to your past history of ductal carcinoma in situ?
Patient: I take coq10, vitamin d, vitamin c, fish oil, and elderberry fruit. I don't have any symptoms related to my past history, and I'm feeling good overall. I do have some back and knee pain, which my doctors say is age-related, and I've been working on lowering my cholesterol through diet and exercise.
Doctor: Please describe the nature, duration, and severity of your back and knee pain, including any factors that aggravate or relieve it.
Patient: The back pain is more of a constant ache, especially in the lower back, and it's been going on for a few years. It gets worse when I stand for long periods or lift things, but it feels a little better when I rest or stretch. The knee pain is similar—mostly in my left knee, and it bothers me when I walk or go up stairs, but I can manage it with some rest.
Doctor: Could you please provide the results of any recent imaging or laboratory tests related to your breast cancer follow-up or the back and knee pain?
Patient: I don't have any recent imaging or lab tests specifically for my back and knee pain, but my last mammogram in January 2021 was normal and showed no signs of recurrence. My primary care doctor is managing my back and knee pain, and they've said it's related to aging. I haven't had any other tests for those issues recently.
Doctor: Could you please confirm if you have any other medical conditions or medications that you are currently taking, and if you have had any recent physical examinations or tests?
Patient: I don't have any other medical conditions besides high cholesterol, which I'm managing through diet and exercise. I take coq10, vitamin d, vitamin c, fish oil, and elderberry fruit, and that's all. I had a physical examination with you today, and my last mammogram was in January 2021, which was normal. I haven't had any other recent tests or exams.
Doctor: Could you please describe any recent changes in your back or knee pain, and whether your current management strategies, such as rest or stretching, have been effective in managing your symptoms?
Patient: The back pain hasn't really changed much—it's still there, but I manage it with rest and stretching. The knee pain is the same, too. I can walk and go up stairs, but it does bother me a bit. I haven't needed any medication for it, and I'm trying to stay active as much as I can.
Doctor: Thank you for sharing that. To ensure we have a complete understanding of your health, could you please tell me if you have any known allergies or have experienced any other symptoms besides the back and knee pain?
Patient: I don't have any known allergies besides penicillin. Other than the back and knee pain, I haven't had any other symptoms or issues recently. I feel generally well and am managing my cholesterol through diet and exercise.
Doctor: Could you please share any recent imaging or lab tests you've had for your back and knee pain, if available?
Patient: I don't have any recent imaging or lab tests specifically for my back and knee pain. My primary care doctor is managing those issues and has said they're related to aging. I haven't had any other tests for those problems recently.
Doctor: Could you please confirm if there are any other symptoms or concerns you would like to discuss during this visit?
Patient: I don't have any other symptoms or concerns to discuss right now. I'm feeling well overall, and I'm happy with the plan to come back in a year after my mammogram in April 2022. Everything seems under control.
